_meta.note: Industry, peers, street, ownership (Jun-2026), moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts for the Craftsman Automation initiation. Only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026.

industry.demand: Craftsman's end markets moved in different directions in FY26-Q1FY27. Indian PVs and 2Ws grew and their makers are building greenfield plants and asking suppliers to follow (CMD: customers announcing 1,500-acre, Rs3,000-20,000 cr sites). Tractors did better; trucks were 'somewhat muted' (Q4 call). Industrial demand turned up: material-handling and storage orders rose quarter on quarter ('the capex cycle started in India', Q1 call). Data-centre and gas-genset demand created a new market for large-engine castings, with global suppliers 'full' on capacity (Q4 call).
industry.aluminium: Aluminium die-casting is fragmented and capital-hungry; global leaders are US$3-6 bn companies and several Indian listed peers from the north and west have plants near Chennai. Customers increasingly want casting plus machining in one place; raw castings 'are not going to be viable' as aluminium, energy, labour and consumables costs rise (CMD, Q4 call). Aluminium is passed through, but with a lag, and some customers 'take their own time' (Q1 call).
industry.costs: Labour is the cost management worries about most: minimum wages are being reset and the new labour codes (notified 21-Nov-2025) raise costs; the CMD expects manpower inflation of ~20% a year in places and says it is 'very difficult to pass on'. Replacement capex costs 5-7x what the same capacity cost in 2016 (land 8-9x, construction 3-4x, machines ~2x in rupees), which raises the entry barrier but also Craftsman's own reinvestment bill.
industry.outsourcing: Engine-block and head machining is being outsourced by OEMs that used to do it in-house, and global engine makers are moving supply to India ('China plus one'); Craftsman has been doing this since the 1990s and built in-house special-purpose machines to keep costs down.

excluded.BHARATFORG: Earnings distorted: exceptional charges in three of the last four quarters (Rs358 cr in Jun-2026, which turned the quarter into a loss), so its ~93x trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 sits on depressed EPS (same exclusion as the Bosch, Motherson, Uno Minda and Sona initiations).
excluded.GABRIEL: No five-year history: Screener's P/E series starts in May-2024 (after Gabriel's restructuring), so there is no five-year median (same exclusion as the Motherson, Uno Minda and Sona initiations).

peers.note: The auto-component peer set of the Bosch, Motherson, Uno Minda and Sona initiations (their union), Craftsman itself left out. SCHAEFFLER (December year-end) has P/E history from Feb-2023, ZFCVINDIA from May-2022 and MSUMI from Apr-2022: their medians cover the history available. Peer multiples at the 30-Sep-2026 close from tools/authoring/asof-peers.js. Listed aluminium die-casters (e.g. Endurance, already in the set) are the closest business peers; tyre and battery makers are left out.

street._note: Notes published 30-Jul to 30-Sep-2026 (Q1FY27 results came on 30-Jul-2026). Full notes are mostly behind logins; Emkay's 31-Jul-2026 note was available as a PDF.

brokers.thesis: Robust Q1 (revenue 9% above estimate); entering a strong growth phase as large-engine castings, Sunbeam's turnaround and new aluminium capacity pay off; re-rating potential. Multiple raised from 15x to 17x; FY27-28E EPS +10%.

All-round beat, but the run-up already prices in the strong delivery and better growth outlook; stock at ~40x FY27E. Neutral since 2024 (targets Rs6,542 at 24x Sep-27E in Nov-2025, Rs7,096 at 25x Dec-27E in Jan-2026).

moat: Process know-how in machining cylinder blocks and heads
35+ years; in-house special-purpose machines; import substitution for critical parts; new large-engine customers took ~4 years to approve it
Parts are validated per programme (1-4 years); switching is slow, but OEMs dual-source and squeeze legacy prices
~95,000 t in FY26 makes it one of India's larger die-casters, but global rivals are 5-10x bigger and casting alone earns little
Replacement capex 5-7x 2016 levels protects installed capacity, but the same inflation hits Craftsman's own expansion
One customer was 24-35% of standalone revenue; aluminium pass-through lags; labour costs hard to pass on
critiques: Returns are low for the capital used: ROCE 12-16% (Screener 14% in FY26) with Rs1,000-1,500 cr of capex a year; two QIPs in two years (Rs3,200 cr) were needed to hold leverage at ~2x net debt/EBITDA.

Growth has been bought as much as built: DR Axion (76% in Feb-2023, the last 24% for Rs250 cr in Jun-2024), Sunbeam (Rs606 cr, loss-making) and the German foundry took aluminium from 21% of revenue (FY21) to 59% (FY26) and diluted the EBITDA margin from 28% to 15%.
Customer concentration: one customer was 35% of standalone revenue in FY25 and 24% in FY26.
Promoter selling and pay: the CMD sold 2% at ~Rs9,250 five days after the QIP at Rs8,700, and his pay rose 112% to Rs11.9 cr in FY26.
Disclosure: segment EBIT but no segment depreciation or EBITDA, no entity-level numbers for Sunbeam or DR Axion, and no order book.
gaps: Annual segment data for FY20 and earlier not collected (FY21 onwards from the annual reports).
Jun-2026 named mutual-fund and FPI holdings: not available to us (only categories and the QIP allottee list).
QIP-2026 issue expenses and the exact split of uses (debt prepayment / capex / working capital) were not public in our sources: we add the gross Rs2,000 cr to cash.
Jun-2026 balance sheet and net debt: not published (Craftsman publishes the balance sheet half-yearly; Sep-2026 numbers came after the as-of date).

Broker notes other than Emkay and Motilal Oswal (Anand Rathi, Avendus Spark, IIFL, Goldman Sachs and others asked questions on the Q1 call) were not visible to us; the S&P consensus (8 analysts, Rs11,371 average, 31-Jul-2026) is shown for reference only.
Sunbeam and DR Axion entity-level revenue and profit for FY26 (AOC-1 shows turnover and profit but we have not reconciled it to segment data).
Value and timing of the Gurgaon (Sunbeam) land sale: the CMD implied ~Rs400 cr (debt 'Rs2,700 cr rather than Rs3,100 cr'); not in our numbers.
conflicts: Company EBITDA (Rs408 cr in Q1FY27, Rs1,300 cr in FY26) includes other income; Screener's (Rs384 cr / Rs1,238 cr) does not. We use Screener's basis throughout.
Promoter block deal: one report calls it a block deal, another an open-market sale; lock-up 180 days vs 18 months in different reports.

Company net debt (~Rs3,100 cr at Mar-26, ND/EBITDA 2.43x) vs Screener's borrowings incl. leases Rs3,623 cr less cash and investments Rs193 cr = Rs3,430 cr: the difference is mainly lease liabilities (Rs283 cr) and bank balances outside cash equivalents.
